page.layout: One page of text, one column, with the running head "EPISTOLA." above it. Below the text a signature block, set right, with the printer's line "Tuæ amplitudini addictissimus / Iacobus Aubertus medicus." Gathering signature at the bottom right.

p.i: unquam à bonis literis & disciplinis te avocare potuit, prohibuitque quominus ingeniosissimè Minervam cum Marte nexu arctissimo coniungeres. Itaque te oro, Generosissime & amplissime vir, ut hæc scripta nostra tibi oblata accipere libenti animo, & benignè digneris, ac in his non tam nos, quàm ipsam naturæ philosophiam audire velis. Deus autem Opt. max. ipsius naturæ creator & dominus te tuámque splendidissimam familiam suis donis præstantissimis, et o-mnigenis ornamentis in dies magis ac magis augeat. Vale. Datum Lau-sannæ Calendis Mart. Anni 1584.

main_text.p:
Tuæ amplitudini addictissimus
Iacobus Aubertus medicus.

page.notes: The first word is a catchless fragment carried over from the previous page, so it is marked cont="true" and "vnquam" is read as "unquam". The "a" of "accipere" and the "m" in "amplissime" are partly covered by an ink blot; they are read from context and are not certain. The stroke between "audire" and "velis" is a printer's mark, not a letter, and is not transcribed. The signature mark at the foot is hard to read and may be "E ij" or "E 2". The faint mirrored text on the page is show-through and is left out.
